conditions: Positive point masses or nonoverlapping spherically symmetric positive masses in Newtonian gravity; r is positive center separation; F is force magnitude.
spoken_aliases: f equals capital g times the fraction with numerator m sub one times m sub two and denominator r squared
gravitational force magnitude equals the gravitational constant times the product of the two masses divided by the square of their separation

evidence: Empirical Newtonian inverse-square law; take the magnitude of the central attractive force. For spherical nonoverlapping positive masses the shell theorem gives the same exterior force as point masses at their centers. This is a model-law check, not a derivation of gravitation from mathematics.
